☁️ NAS Backup (Tailscale)
Push your full data to your Synology over Tailscale. Credentials stay on this device only — they are never included in exported/synced backup files.
🔒 If set, the backup is encrypted on this device before upload — unreadable on the NAS (or by whoever runs it) without this passphrase. It never leaves this device. Lose it and the backup can't be recovered.

🔧 Training Preferences
Advanced sets
Auto-assigns Drop Set, Failure & Rest-Pause by focus, and seeds antagonist supersets. Turn off for clean Work + Warm-Up only.
Auto-rotate splits 🔄
Picks each gym day's split automatically by muscle recovery — rotating through all eight splits and never stacking the same muscles two days running. Overrides your fixed weekly schedule. Turn off to follow the schedule you set below.
Auto-superset pairing
Automatically pairs antagonist exercises (e.g. Lat Pull-Down ↔ Pec Fly) when Advanced sets is on. Turn off to manage supersets manually.
Warmup sets
Auto-generates two warmup rows (40% + 65%) on compound exercises. Turn off if you warm up independently before your session.
Auto rest timer
Starts the rest countdown automatically when you complete a set. Turn off to manage your own rest -- the timer stays accessible but won't fire.
Smart workout note
Shows the blue info banner explaining today's advanced set types. Turn off if you already know what Drop Sets and Rest-Pause mean.
Run & Marathon mode
Enables run days, the Marathon tab, and run logging. Turn off during gym-only phases (winter, post-race recovery). Run history is preserved.
Net carbs mode
Display net carbs (total carbs − fiber) instead of total carbs across the nutrition page. Useful for keto, low-carb, and diabetic tracking.
Rest timer sound
Plays an audible chime when your rest timer hits zero. Useful for eyes-free resting between sets. Turn off for silent gym sessions or when using your own music/podcasts.
Plate loading display
Shows the plates you need to load for each working set alongside the total weight — e.g. "2×45 + 1×25 per side". Helpful if you're still learning bar math.
Show muscle group badges
Displays primary muscle group tags on each exercise row in your workout. Useful for learning anatomy. Turn off for a cleaner, more compact workout view.
📊 TDEE & NUTRITION TARGETS
🔥 WHAT IS TDEE?
Total Daily Energy Expenditure (TDEE) is an estimate of how many calories your body burns in a full day — accounting for your metabolism at rest plus the calories burned through movement and training.
It is calculated using the Mifflin–St Jeor equation for Basal Metabolic Rate (BMR), then multiplied by an activity factor based on your selected activity level. This gives you your maintenance calories — the amount you need to eat to stay at the same weight.
⚖️ HOW TO USE TDEE
• Eat at TDEE → maintain current weight
• Eat 300–500 cal below TDEE → lose ~0.5–1 lb/week
• Eat 200–400 cal above TDEE → lean muscle gain
• Your Nutrition page calorie budget is set to your TDEE automatically
🥩 PROTEIN TARGET
Your protein target is set at 0.85g per pound of bodyweight — the middle of the science-backed 0.7–1.0g/lb range for people who strength train regularly.
Adequate protein: preserves muscle when in a calorie deficit, supports muscle growth during surplus, aids in recovery between sessions, and keeps you fuller longer.
📌 ACTIVITY LEVELS EXPLAINED
Sedentary (×1.2) — Desk job, minimal movement outside gym sessions
Lightly Active (×1.375) — 1–3 gym days, otherwise mostly sitting
Moderately Active (×1.55) — 3–5 training days, some walking daily
Very Active (×1.725) — 6–7 training days, physical job, or marathon training
Note: TDEE is an estimate. Adjust your calorie intake based on real-world results over 2–3 weeks.
🧬 ADAPTIVE CALORIE ENGINE
WHY IT BEATS A FORMULA
The Mifflin–St Jeor formula is a population average — your real metabolism can run 200–400 cal higher or lower. This engine learns your actual maintenance calories from what really happens when you eat and weigh in.
THE MATH
Across your last 3 weeks it compares average calories eaten against your weight trend:
TDEE ≈ avg intake − (weekly weight change × 500)
Your weigh-ins are fit with a regression line so day-to-day water swings don\'t throw it off.
USING IT
It needs ~10 well-logged food days plus 10+ days of weigh-ins to start, and confidence climbs as you log more. Flip the toggle on to make your daily calorie goal follow this number instead of the formula — it recalibrates automatically every time you log.
💪 STRENGTH PROFILE
⚖️ RELATIVE STRENGTH
Your working weight for 3-4 solid sets. Used to personalise weight suggestions across all exercises.
ℹ️ HOW 1RM IS CALCULATED
Uses Epley's formula: 1RM = weight × (1 + reps ÷ 30). For a working weight (typically 7-8 reps at 80%), this estimates your one-rep maximum. Your actual 1RM may vary ±10%. Use the Test Max tab to calculate from any rep count.
Enter the weight you lifted and how many reps you completed. I'll calculate your estimated 1RM and update your profile.

⏱️ INTERVAL TIMER — GUIDE
💡 What it is
A countdown timer that alternates timed work and rest periods for a set number of rounds, with audio cues so you never have to watch the clock. Use it for conditioning finishers, cardio intervals, or any work/rest circuit.
🏷️ The Four Presets
Tabata · 20s work / 10s rest × 8 (4 min)
Short, brutal, all-out bursts with tiny rests. Go as hard as you can each 20-second work period. Best for one movement (bike, burpees, squats, kettlebell swings).
HIIT · 40s work / 20s rest × 10
High-Intensity Interval Training — longer hard efforts with partial recovery. Hard but sustainable across all rounds. Great for circuits of 1–2 exercises or cardio machines.
EMOM · 60s work / 0s rest × 10
Every Minute On the Minute — at the top of each minute do a fixed set (e.g. 10 reps), then rest whatever time is left in that minute. Faster you work, more you rest. Self-pacing strength-conditioning.
Sprints · 30s hard / 90s easy × 6
Near-maximal efforts with long, full recovery so each sprint is high quality. Built for running/cycling sprints or pushing a sled — speed and power, not exhaustion.
🏋️ On Gym Days
Run it as a finisher after lifting (Tabata or HIIT on a bike, rower, or bodyweight move) for a quick conditioning hit, or as EMOM for accessory work without watching rest times.
🏃 On Run Days
Use Sprints for treadmill or track repeats (hard / easy), or HIIT for shorter speed work. The long rest in the Sprints preset keeps each effort fast. Always warm up first.
🌿 Rest days: skip it — keep recovery days easy. Use the rest-day recovery protocols and breathwork instead. (That's why this button is hidden on rest days.)
⚙️ Custom: any preset just fills in the Prep / Work / Rest / Rounds boxes — tweak them freely and the app remembers your last setup.
